checks.detail: FAILS for videos whose stored source_url already carries a t= parameter. Group 11 (by8wrrXW3So, 'What AI Engineer JOBS Need on a Resume') displays 1:13-2:27 and labels the link 'open at 1:13', but the href ends up with TWO t params and URLSearchParams.get('t') returns '51s' - YouTube honours the first, so the link opens at 0:51, 22s early. ThemesView.tsx:19 appends '&t=<n>s' to source_url without stripping an existing t. 8 of 53 corpus videos are affected. Groups 0 and 3 (no pre-existing t) are exact.

notes: ENVIRONMENT: chromium.launch() times out on this machine (wedged Metal compiler XPC service), so demo/validate/v4_themes.py could not be executed through Playwright. Every assertion in that file was executed instead as the equivalent DOM query against the running app in an already-open Chrome at http://127.0.0.1:8021, and the results are what this verdict records. Previous slices (v2_filter, v3_critique) recorded the same constraint the same way.

Layout width was varied by constraining .app rather than by resizing the window (the extension's resize did not change innerWidth, which stayed at 1723px). Clipping was measured at layout widths 1440, 1000 and 820px - the last is below the 900px media-query breakpoint where .th-layout collapses to one column.

'.th-chunkpreview' is deliberately white-space: nowrap and is excluded from the clipping probe: it is a fixed-length collapsed excerpt whose full text is one click away in .th-chunkbody. That is the only nowrap field in the theme CSS and the comment at styles.ts:135 says so explicitly.

The timestamp defect is not new to V4: frontend/src/pipeline/VideoDetail.tsx:18, KnowledgeGraphView.tsx:22 and pipeline/graph.ts:123 build the URL the same way. src/rag/packs.py:574 builds it correctly from video_id and start_seconds.

The frontend gate is the only one of the four gate items this file covers. Cluster spread, property purity, the intruder probe and determinism were checked against the artifact and the stored embeddings, not through the UI.
